If the card is being installed, this rule only applies as indicated by section 8.5.13.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: When a card is moved from one zone to another, the move is instantaneous. The card is never in both zones at once, and it is never not in any zone at all.

A card that is not in any zone is outside the game. Cards outside of the game are distinct from cards in the removed-from-game zone, and cannot affect the game. They can only be affected by abilities that explicitly bring in extra cards from outside the game. See section 1.5.

A public zone is one where cards are freely visible to both players unless they are facedown. The play area, the bank, the set-aside zone, the removed-from-game zone, and both players' score areas and discard piles are public zones. See section 1.21 for rules on card visibility and section 8.1 for rules on the faceup and facedown status of a card.
A hidden zone is one where cards are not visible to either player. Each player's deck is a hidden zone.
A secret zone is one where cards are visible only to their controller. Each player's hand is a secret zone.
A location is a specific position within a zone that an object can occupy. A destination is a location to which an object is to be moved.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: A card in a player's deck has a location identified by how many cards it is from the top of that deck.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Some objects in the play area are in specific locations. See section 4.6.5.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The location of a hosted object is its host card.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: All other objects are simply located in their zone and do not have a more specific location.
When the game begins, each player's deck presented during setup becomes their in-game draw deck.
Decks must be kept facedown with their cards hidden from both players. Neither player may look at the cards in any deck without being explicitly directed to do so by a rule or card ability.
Decks are ordered. The location of each card in a deck must be maintained except when a player is explicitly directed to manipulate the cards in a deck by a rule or card ability. See rule 4.1.7a.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: While searching a deck, a player is not required to maintain the order of the searched cards or indicate the previous location of any card found by the search. Note that the deck is always shuffled upon completion of the search, as required by rule 8.7.3.
The number of cards in a deck is open information. Any player may count the number of cards in a deck at any time.
Cards in a deck are inactive.
Each player's deck has its own name as a means of differentiating between the two.
R&D

rules.label: a.
rules.text: R&D is the name for the Corp's deck. It is also one of the Corp's central servers. See section 4.6.7.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If the Corp must ever draw from R&D while it is empty, the Runner wins the game. See section 1.7.
Stack

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The stack is the name for the Runner's deck.

A player's hand is the zone in which they hold the cards they have drawn from their deck. Cards can be added to a player's hand by other rules and card abilities as well. During setup, each player draws a starting hand. See section 1.6.
A player's hand is kept secret from their opponent. A player may look at the cards in their own hand, but not at any of the cards in their opponent's hands.
Hands are not ordered. A player may freely arrange the cards in their hand in any order at any time.
The number of cards in a hand is open information to all players. Any player may count the number of cards in a hand at any time.
Cards in a hand are inactive.

Each player has a maximum hand size, usually five. A player may have any number of cards in their hand at any given time, but during the discard phase of a player's turn they must discard cards from their hand until there are no more cards in their hand than their maximum hand size allows. See section 5.5.
Each player's hand has its own name as a means of differentiating between the two.
HQ

rules.label: a.
rules.text: HQ is the name for the Corp's hand. It is also one of the Corp's central servers. See section 4.6.7.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Corp's identity card represents their HQ server for the purposes of gameplay. Ice protecting HQ is installed in front of the Corp's identity card and upgrades installed in the root of HQ are installed behind the Corp's identity card.
Grip

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The grip is the name for the Runner's hand.
A player's discard pile is the zone in which they place cards that have been trashed or discarded. Discard piles start the game empty.
Discard piles are not ordered. A player may freely arrange the cards in their discard pile in any order at any time.
The number of cards in a discard pile is open information. Any player may count the number of cards in a discard pile at any time.
Cards in a discard pile are inactive.
Each player's discard pile has its own name as a means of differentiating between the two.
Archives

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Archives is the name for the Corp's discard pile. It is also one of the Corp's central servers. See section 4.6.7.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Cards in Archives can be either faceup or facedown. If a Corp card is visible to the Runner when it is trashed or discarded, it is put in Archives faceup. If a Corp card is not visible to the Runner when it is trashed or discarded, then it is put in Archives facedown. Facedown cards in Archives should be oriented horizontally so that the Runner can easily see they are present.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The faceup cards in Archives are open information. Any player may look through the faceup cards in Archives at any time. The facedown cards in Archives are visible only to the Corp. The Corp may look through the facedown cards in Archives at any time, but the Runner cannot look at them.
Heap

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The heap is the name for the Runner's discard pile.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The cards in the heap are open information. Any player may look through the cards in the heap at any time.
A player's score area is the zone in which they place agendas they have scored or stolen. Section 1.17 details scoring and stealing agendas. Score areas start the game empty.
The agendas in a score area are open information. A player may look through or count the agendas in a score area at any time.
Score areas are not ordered. A player may freely arrange the agendas in their score area in any order at any time.
Agendas in the Corp's score area are active. Agendas in the Runner's score area are inactive unless stated otherwise.
The play area is the shared active zone into which cards are played or installed. The play area normally starts the game empty except for each of the player's identities.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Section 1.5 details cases where an ability may cause cards to start the game in the play area.
The number of cards in the play area and the location of each card in the play area is always open information.

Whether or not a card itself and its attributes are open information while in the play area is determined by the card's status. Cards that are faceup are open information and can be examined by any player at any time. Cards that are facedown are secret information and can only be examined by the player who controls the card. See section 10.2.
Whether or not a card is active while in the play area is determined by the card's status.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Identities start the game in the play area and are always active.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Generally, Corp agendas, assets, ice, and upgrades are installed into the play area unrezzed and thus inactive. They are active while rezzed. See section 8.5.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Generally, Runner hardware, programs, and resources are installed into the play area faceup and active. See section 8.5.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Some Runner cards are installed facedown or turned facedown through card abilities. This is distinct from the status of rezzed/unrezzed that Corp cards can have. Facedown Runner cards are not active. See section 8.1.4.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: Operations and events are played into the play area faceup and are active for the duration of their resolution before being trashed. See section 8.6.
Some objects in the play area are organized into specific orientations and/or locations.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Corp cards are arranged into distinct servers. Agendas and assets are installed in the roots of remote servers, upgrades are installed in the roots of any servers, and pieces of ice are installed horizontally protecting servers. See section 4.6.6 and section 4.6.9.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Corp's identity is used to indicate where in the play area HQ exists for the purposes of installing upgrades in the root of HQ and ice protecting HQ. See section 4.6.7.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Runner's identity, hardware, programs, and resources do not have specific locations in the play area.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: There is no specific location in the play area for operations or events. They are simply played into the play area, where they resolve before being trashed. See section 8.6.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: Credits in the play area are always placed in a designated location: the Corp's credit pool, the Runner's credit pool, the bad publicity fund, or hosted on a card. See section 1.10 for information about credit pools, and see section 10.6 for information about the bad publicity fund.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: Tag counters and bad publicity counters have no specific location in the play area unless hosted on a card. Other types of counters are either nonfunctional gameplay aids or appear only in host relationships. See also section 1.9.

rules.label: g.
rules.text: Some cards can act as install locations for other cards while in the play area, such that cards of a specific type can be hosted directly onto them during the installation process. In this type of host relationship, both the host card and the hosted card are in the play area, but the host relationship can affect certain aspects of either the card or the installation process. See section 1.13.

rules.label: h.
rules.text: Some cards can host other cards without installing them. In this type of host relationship, both the host card and the hosted card are in the play area, but the hosted card is not installed and thus not active. See section 1.13.
Servers

rules.label: a.
rules.text: A server is a set of locations where the Corp installs their cards into the play area and against which the Runner can initiate runs. Whenever a Corp installs an agenda, asset, ice, or upgrade, they must choose a destination server for that card. See section 8.5.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Once a Corp card is installed, it cannot be moved from its server without explicit direction from a game rule or card effect.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The two types of servers are central servers and remote servers. See sections 4.6.7 and 4.6.8, respectively.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: All servers can have ice installed protecting them. See section 4.6.9.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: All servers have a root where cards can be installed. A central server's root can contain any number of upgrades, while a remote server's root can contain 1 asset or agenda and any number of upgrades. Assets and agendas cannot be installed in the root of a central server.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: All cards installed in the root of a server are kept in the same orientation and location together. The order in which the cards are installed is open information, but the type of cards installed in the root of a remote server should not be derivable from their orientation or location.

rules.label: g.
rules.text: Only 1 region upgrade can be installed in the root of a server at a time. See section 3.6.5.

rules.label: h.
rules.text: Some upgrades have restrictions limiting them to specific servers. See rule 8.5.12.

rules.label: i.
rules.text: Some cards refer to the server where they are located (or the central server corresponding to the zone where they are located) using the phrase "this server". If an ability is initiated by a trigger condition or cost involving the ability's source card moving from a server, its root, or protecting it to another server or to a location not associated with any server, treat "this server" as referring to the server associated with the previous location of the card throughout resolution of that ability. If an ability moves its source card while it is resolving, continue to interpret "this server" based on the card's previous location.

rules.label: j.
rules.text: If an ability on a card currently or previously located in a server, its root, or protecting it refers to "another server", this means any server except "this server" as interpreted by rule 4.6.6i. If a card's abilities involve choosing a server, "another server" in a linked ability means any server except the chosen server. If neither of the previous cases apply and a run is in progress, "another server" means any server except the attacked server.

rules.label: k.
rules.text: If an ability on an object uses the phrase "this server", and that object is hosted on another object (see section 1.13), the server referred to is the server of the host object.
Central Servers

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Corp has three central servers at all times. Each central server corresponds to one of the Corp's zones: HQ corresponds to the Corp's hand, R&D corresponds to the Corp's deck, and Archives corresponds to the Corp's discard pile.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Corp's identity is in the play area to indicate the location of HQ relative to other servers, but it is not in HQ, in the root of HQ, or protecting HQ. The cards in HQ are held in the Corp's hand. The upgrades installed in the root of HQ are placed in a vertical orientation near the Corp's identity. The ice installed protecting HQ are placed in a horizontal orientation in front of the Corp's identity outwards towards the Runner.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Corp's deck is placed in the play area to indicate the location of R&D relative to other servers, but the cards in the deck are not installed. The cards in R&D are the cards in the deck. The upgrades installed in the root of R&D are placed in a vertical orientation near the deck. The ice installed protecting R&D are placed in a horizontal orientation in front of the deck outwards towards the Runner.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Corp's discard pile is placed in the play area to indicate the location of Archives relative to other servers, but the cards in the discard pile are not installed. The cards in Archives are the cards in the discard pile. The upgrades installed in the root of Archives are placed in a vertical orientation near the discard pile. The ice installed protecting Archives are placed in a horizontal orientation in front of the discard pile outwards towards the Runner.
Remote Servers

rules.label: a.
rules.text: A remote server is the only type of server that can contain an asset or agenda in its root.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Corp starts the game with no remote servers. The Corp creates a new remote server by declaring it as the destination server for a card they are about to install. There is usually no limit to the number of remote servers the Corp can have at any given time.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Cards installed in the roots of separate remote servers are placed in a vertical orientation in a row extending away from the central servers to indicate the locations of the remote servers relative to other servers. The ice installed protecting each remote server are placed in a horizontal orientation in front of any cards in the root of that server, outwards towards the Runner.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: A remote server exists as long as there is at least one card in the root of or protecting it. A remote server can be made up of only ice protecting it, only cards installed in it, or a combination of both.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: During checkpoints, a remote server ceases to exist if there are no cards installed in its root and no cards installed protecting it. If a server ceases to exist during a run against it, then the run ends after any currently open paid ability window closes. Unless the run has already been declared either successful or unsuccessful, it is neither. See rule 8.5.8.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: Some abilities limit the number of remote servers. While such an ability is active, the Corp cannot create a new remote server if this would raise the total number of remote servers above the specified limit. During step 10.3.1e of each checkpoint, if there are more remote servers than an active limit allows, the Corp player chooses a number of servers equal to the limit. The checkpoint then trashes all cards in the root of and protecting each remote server that was not chosen.
Protecting a Server

rules.label: a.
rules.text: An installed piece of ice is arranged in a horizontal position in front of the server it is protecting. Ice are ordered within the play area. The location of a piece of ice is defined by the server it is protecting and the number of other pieces of ice between it and the server.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If there is no other ice between the server and a piece of ice, that ice is the innermost piece of ice. If there is no ice farther from the server than a piece of ice, that ice is the outermost piece of ice. If there is only one piece of ice protecting a server, that ice is both the innermost and the outermost piece of ice.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If two pieces of ice protecting two different servers share the same number of ice between them and their respective servers, those pieces of ice are considered to be in the same position.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: When the Corp installs a piece of ice protecting a server, they must place it in the outermost position protecting that server. See section 8.5.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: If the number of other ice between a piece of ice and the server changes, its position will change accordingly, moving either closer or farther from the server. If this occurs while that ice is being approached, encountered, or passed during a run, the Runner's position attacking the server changes in the same way.
The bank is an inactive zone shared by both players. It holds an unlimited supply of counters for use during gameplay.
Counters placed or loaded onto a card are taken from the bank unless otherwise specified. Counters gained by players are taken from the bank unless otherwise specified.
Credits and other counters that are spent to pay costs return to the bank.
Counters that are not in a legal location return to the bank during checkpoints. See section 10.3.
Cards are never located in the bank.
The set-aside zone is an inactive zone shared by both players. It is used as a temporary holding space for objects being affected by abilities.
If an object is "set aside", it is moved from its current zone to the set-aside zone.

An ability cannot see the set-aside zone unless it specifically sets objects aside or refers to set-aside objects. Outside of these cases, cards moved into another zone from the set-aside zone are treated as though they entered that zone directly from their location prior to being set aside.
Cards found during a search are set aside facedown while the search completes (in particular, while any deck that was searched is shuffled). See section 8.7.

Some paid abilities with a trigger cost that uninstalls or forfeits the ability's source card need to refer to or act on that card's hosted cards or counters. These abilities set aside the hosted cards or counters as the trigger cost is paid. See rule 9.5.5.
Cards set aside by a card ability are faceup unless the ability specifically instructs that they be set aside facedown.

Facedown cards in the set-aside zone must be kept in distinct groups according to the effect that sets them aside. Cards within such a group are not ordered and can be freely arranged by their controller.
The removed-from-game zone is an inactive zone shared by both players. It is used to take cards out of any player's control until the end of the game.
If a card is removed from the game, it is moved from its current zone to the removed-from-game zone.
Forfeiting an agenda removes it from the game. See rule 8.2.5.
Cards that have been removed from the game are inactive.
A card that has been removed from the game cannot move out of the removed-from-game zone or otherwise be interacted with.
Cards that have been removed from the game are open information. Any player may look through or count the cards that have been removed from the game at any time.
A turn is a duration of time during which a player may take actions and is the first to receive priority to act during priority windows.

The Corp's turn consists of three phases. During the draw phase, the Corp draws the top card of R&D into HQ; during the action phase, the Corp spends [click]s to perform actions; during the discard phase, the Corp discards until the number of cards in HQ does not exceed their maximum hand size. Once the Corp's turn ends, the Runner's turn begins.

The Runner's turn consists of two phases. During the action phase, the Runner spends [click]s to perform actions; during the discard phase, the Runner discards until the number of cards in their grip does not exceed their maximum hand size. Once the Runner's turn ends, the Corp's turn begins.
The beginning and end of each player's turn are formalized as particular steps of the turn timing structures.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Trigger conditions related to a turn beginning are not met as the turn timing structure opens. They are met at the timing step that indicates the formal beginning of the turn.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Trigger conditions related to a turn or discard phase ending are met at the timing step that indicates the formal end of the turn. They are not met when the turn timing structure later closes. The end of the turn and the end of the discard phase are the same.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Some effects can occur before the "turn begins" step or after the "turn ends" step of a turn. The player whose turn timing structure is in progress is still the active player, and effects that apply during their turn are still applicable, even though their turn has not yet formally begun or has already formally ended.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Once the game begins, it is always one or the other player's turn. There is no time "between turns".
An action is any paid ability where the cost begins with a [click] symbol.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Other costs can contain [click] symbols without denoting an action.
A player initiates an action by paying its cost in [click], as well as any other costs associated with that action, during their action window.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Once an action is initiated, it must be completed before the game can advance to the next step or open another action window. If the effects of an action initiate a timing structure, such as a run, players may use paid abilities, rez cards, and score agendas as dictated by the priority windows of that nested timing structure, but otherwise players cannot perform any of those voluntary effects while the action is resolving. See section 9.2 for more details about priority.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If a timing structure is initiated during the resolution of an action, that action is not complete until the new timing structure is complete and any further effects of the initiated action following the completion of the new timing structure are resolved.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: A conditional ability that meets its trigger condition due to a player taking an action resolves after the action's trigger cost is paid, before the effects of the action itself. See rule 9.1.2a.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Some conditional abilities meet their trigger conditions due to an action "ending", "finishing", or "completing". These abilities resolve in the reaction window following step 5.6.2b or step 5.7.1f, for actions taken by the Corp and Runner, respectively.
Each player has several basic actions they can always perform. The Corp's basic actions are listed in section 5.2.6, and the Runner's basic actions are listed in section 5.2.7.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If an ability has a trigger condition related to an effect being performed “with the basic action”, that trigger condition is met by any basic action that performs the indicated effect. If an ability imposes a cost on performing an effect “with the basic action”, that cost applies to any instance of the indicated effect that would occur as part of resolving a basic action.
A player can only take actions during the action phase of their turn. If an effect directs a player to take an action outside of that player's action phase, instead that player does nothing.
Some cards refer to players taking "the same action" or "different actions".

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Actions a player performs are the same if they are all the same basic action or if all of those actions were initiated by the same ability from the same card.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Actions a player performs are different if each of them is initiated from a different basic action or card ability. Instances of equivalent abilities on different cards are still different actions.
Corp Actions

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The following basic actions are always available to the Corp during their action phase, in addition to any actions provided by card abilities.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: "[click]: Gain 1[credit]."

rules.label: c.
rules.text: "[click]: Draw 1 card."

rules.label: d.
rules.text: "[click]: Install 1 agenda, asset, upgrade, or piece of ice from HQ." See section 8.5.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: "[click]: Play 1 operation from HQ." See section 8.6.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: "[click], 1[credit]: Advance 1 installed card." See section 1.18.

rules.label: g.
rules.text: "[click], 2[credit]: Trash 1 resource. Take this action only if the Runner is tagged." See section 10.5.

rules.label: h.
rules.text: "[click][click][click]: Purge virus counters." See rule 10.1.2.
Runner Actions

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The following basic actions are always available to the Runner during their action phase, in addition to any actions provided by card abilities.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: "[click]: Gain 1[credit]."

rules.label: c.
rules.text: "[click]: Draw 1 card."

rules.label: d.
rules.text: "[click]: Install 1 program, resource, or piece of hardware from the grip." See section 8.5.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: "[click]: Play 1 event from the grip." See section 8.6.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: "[click]: Run any server." See section 6.

rules.label: g.
rules.text: "[click], 2[credit]: Remove 1 tag." See section 10.5.
The draw phase is the first phase of the Corp's turn. It includes the formal beginning of the Corp's turn and the Corp's mandatory draw.
The mandatory draw is a card draw performed by the Corp. It is not an action and does not cost [click].
The Runner's turn does not have a draw phase.
The action phase is the first phase of the Runner's turn and the second phase of the Corp's turn. It is the only timing structure in which players can take actions, as discussed in section 5.2.

During a player's action phase, they must continue to take actions until they have no more clicks or the phase is ended directly by a card ability. The player may take actions in any combination and order as long as they pay the appropriate costs. Once they have no remaining clicks, the action phase ends.
A player's action phase can be forced to end by certain card abilities (e.g. via the ability on a terminal operation or event). When a player's action phase is forced to end, the following occurs:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The current step of the action phase ends, and all remaining steps are skipped.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Any currently open priority windows close, their associated abilities lose their pending status, and the player with priority loses priority.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Any currently resolving actions or abilities cease resolving and are considered complete.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Conditions related to the action phase ending are met, and a checkpoint occurs. A reaction window created by this checkpoint is still considered to be taking place in the action phase, but players cannot take actions during this window.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: After completing any reaction windows opened by the checkpoint from rule 5.4.3d, the game proceeds to the active player's discard phase.
If an effect attempts to end a player's action phase during their draw phase, their discard phase, or another player's turn, this effect does nothing.
The discard phase is the last phase of each player's turn. It contains the discard step and the formal end of that player's turn.
discarding is the act by which a player moves a card to their discard pile during their discard phase if they have exceeded their maximum hand size.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Cards discarded from HQ are always sent to Archives facedown, regardless of whether they have been previously accessed by the Runner.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A discarded card is not considered to have been trashed, and vice versa.
A player's maximum hand size is the maximum number of cards that player can keep in their hand during their discard phase.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Players begin the game with a maximum hand size of five cards.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Each point of core damage the Runner suffers permanently reduces their maximum hand size by 1 card. See section 10.4. Other abilities can modify a player's maximum hand size directly.
The discard step is step 5.6.3a for the Corp, and step 5.7.2a for the Runner. In that step, the active player discards cards to reach their maximum hand size.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Before the Runner discards cards in their discard step, they must check for a flatline. See rule 1.7.2b.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If the number of cards in the active player's hand is less than or equal to their maximum hand size, nothing else happens in this step.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If the number of cards in the active player's hand is greater than their maximum hand size, they discard a number of cards from their hand equal to the difference. The discarding player chooses which of their cards to discard, and the chosen cards are all discarded simultaneously.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If an effect instructs a player to skip their discard step, the game proceeds directly from the start of their discard phase to the step following the discard step. They will not check their hand size or discard cards.
During the draw phase, the following steps occur in order:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Corp gains their allotted clicks (default [click][click][click]).

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities, the Corp may rez non-ice cards, and the Corp may score agendas. (P) (R) (S)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Corp's recurring credits ([recurring]) refill.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Corp's turn formally begins. Conditions related to the turn beginning are met.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: The Corp performs their mandatory draw.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: The Corp's draw phase is complete. Play proceeds to the Corp's action phase.
During the Corp's action phase, the following steps occur in order:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities, the Corp may rez non-ice cards, and the Corp may score agendas. (P) (R) (S)

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If the Corp has any unspent [click], the Corp takes an action. Otherwise, skip to (d).

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Return to (a).

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Corp's action phase formally ends. Conditions related to the action phase ending are met.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: The Corp's action phase is complete. Play proceeds to the Corp's discard phase.
During the Corp's discard phase, the following steps occur in order:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Corp discards cards to reach their maximum hand size.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. (P) (R)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If the Corp has any unspent [click], the Corp loses those [click].

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Corp's turn formally ends. Conditions related to the turn or discard phase ending are met.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: The Corp's discard phase and turn are complete. Play proceeds to the Runner's turn.
During the Runner's action phase, the following steps occur in order:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Runner gains allotted clicks (default [click][click][click][click]).

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. (P) (R)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Runner's recurring credits ([recurring]) refill.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Runner's turn formally begins. Conditions related to the turn beginning are met.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. (P) (R)

rules.label: f.
rules.text: If the Runner has any unspent [click], the Runner takes an action. Otherwise, skip to (h).

rules.label: g.
rules.text: Return to (e).

rules.label: h.
rules.text: The Runner's action phase formally ends. Conditions related to the action phase ending are met.

rules.label: i.
rules.text: The Runner's action phase is complete. Play proceeds to the Runner's discard phase.
During the Runner's discard phase, the following steps occur in order:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Runner discards cards to reach their maximum hand size.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. (P) (R)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If the Runner has any unspent [click], the Runner loses those [click].

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Runner's turn formally ends. Conditions related to the turn or discard phase ending are met.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: The Runner's discard phase and turn are complete. Play proceeds to the Corp's turn.

A run is a Runner's attack on a server. There are 6 phases used in the procedure of carrying out a run, described in sections 6.3 through 6.8. A run always begins with the Initiation Phase. Section 6.9 contains the full set of steps carried out during each phase, and should be referred to in conjunction with the sections discussing the phases.
The attacked server is the server the Runner is attempting to reach, usually to breach that server.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Runner announces the attacked server in the initiation phase of the run.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Card abilities can sometimes change the attacked server during the run. This does not end the run, but it can affect whether or not certain card abilities or effects apply.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If an ability changes the Runner's position, the attacked server and the current timing step of the run could also change. See section 6.2.8.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: A few abilities change the attacked server directly, without referring to the Runner's position. These abilities do not change the current timing step of the run.

Many abilities modify the sequence of steps taken to resolve a run. Such abilities can direct players to skip steps or phases, replace steps with other effects, move directly from the current timing point to a new phase, or make other changes to the procedures explained in this section. Heed the Golden Rules in section 1.2.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Some abilities direct the Runner to approach or encounter a piece of ice as part of moving them to that ice's position. See section 6.2.8.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: One card, Code Replicator, directs the Runner to approach the piece of ice in their position without first moving them to a new position. This effect changes the current timing step of the run to step 6.9.2, the Approach Ice Phase.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: An ability that directs the Runner to encounter a piece of ice without first moving the Runner's position does not change the current timing point of the run, the attacked server, or the Runner's position. The effect of such an ability is to resolve an Encounter Ice Phase independent of the current state of the run. See section 6.5.9.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Any time the current timing step of the run is moved to a different phase of the run, except for an instruction to end the run (See section 6.1.4, below), no more steps in the previously-active phase are carried out. If a paid ability window is open, players complete that window normally. Then the active phase is complete and a checkpoint occurs. Finally, the game proceeds to the new phase.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: If a condition refers to encountering a piece of ice "after" an approach or passing a piece of ice "after" an encounter, then that condition is only met by the indicated phases or steps occurring in direct sequence according to the standard progression of the run.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: If a condition refers to passing a piece of ice "after" fully breaking it, then that condition is only met when the Runner passes that piece of ice after an encounter (as defined by rule 6.1.3e), and only if the Runner fully broke that ice during that encounter. See section 6.5.7.

To end the run is to halt the Runner's progress toward the server. When an effect ends the run, the current phase of the run ends without following any of its remaining steps, and before completing open priority windows. The game immediately moves from the current timing point to step 6.9.6, the Run Ends Phase.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a run is in progress, an instruction to end the run also ends any breach and/or access taking place.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If an instruction to end the run resolves while there is no run in progress, but there is an encounter in progress, that encounter ends without resolving any more of its steps. Process any open priority windows in the same way as described in section 6.8.2, but do not resolve any other steps of the Run Ends Phase. Any breach and/or access initiated during the encounter also ends, but a breach and/or access that was already in progress when the encounter began is not ended.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If an instruction to end the run resolves while there is neither a run nor an encounter in progress, that effect does nothing.

Jacking out is the process by which a Runner voluntarily ends a run. Jacking out follows the usual process for ending the run as described in section 6.1.4, but some card abilities function differently depending on whether or not the Runner chose to end the run by jacking out.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Runner has the opportunity to jack out after passing a piece of ice.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If there is no ice protecting the server, the Runner has the opportunity to jack out before approaching the server.
Each server has a sequence of positions that assign an order to ice protecting that server. A piece of ice protecting a server always occupies exactly 1 position in that server's sequence at a time.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: A piece of ice that is hosted on another card is not protecting a server and does not occupy a position, regardless of whether the ice is installed.

When a piece of ice is installed protecting a server or an installed piece of ice is moved, a new position is created for that ice. For ice being installed, the position is created when the Corp declares an install destination for the ice (step 8.5.16b), and the ice occupies that position once the ice becomes installed (step 8.5.16e). For installed ice being moved, the position is created when the movement happens, and the ice occupies that position immediately.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is being installed in or moved to the outermost position protecting a server, the new position is outward from the outermost already-existing position. If an instruction to install a piece of ice does not explicitly specify otherwise, the ice is installed in the outermost position.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is being installed in or moved to the innermost position protecting a server, the new position is inward from the innermost already-existing position.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is being installed "directly inward" from another piece of ice, the new position is inward from that ice's position, and outward from the next already-existing position inward, if there is one.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is being installed "in any position", the new position can be created outward from all existing positions, inward from all existing positions, or between any two existing consecutive positions, as the Corp chooses.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: One card, Mutate, has an ability that installs a piece of ice in the "same position" as a particular piece of ice that was previously trashed. This is a different usage of "same position" from that described in rule 6.2.3. For this installation, the ice is installed protecting the same server the trashed ice was protecting, and the new position is created at the same place in that server's sequence of positions as the position the trashed ice had.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is swapped with a piece of ice protecting a server, no new position is created. The first ice will occupy the position previously held by the second ice (and vice-versa, if the first piece of ice was also protecting a server).

Some abilities refer to ice in the "same position" protecting different servers. Two pieces of ice occupy the "same position" if their respective servers have the same number of positions inward from their respective positions.

If a piece of ice leaves its position, except by being swapped with another piece of ice, its former position ceases to exist. This happens during step 10.3.1i of the next checkpoint, unless the Runner is in that position, in which case the position continues to exist until the Runner moves to another position or ceases to have a position.
During a run, the Runner occupies the attacked server's positions.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Runner enters the outermost position protecting the attacked server at step 6.9.1d of the Initiation Phase.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Runner progresses through the positions of the attacked server in order. While the Runner occupies a position, they approach, encounter (if the ice is rezzed), and pass the ice in that position, then they proceed to the next position moving inward, until they complete this process for the innermost position or the run is ended.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Once the Runner leaves the innermost position protecting a server, they no longer have a position. This occurs at step 6.9.4d of the Movement Phase. However, abilities can still move the Runner to a position later in that phase.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: During the Success Phase and the Run Ends Phase, the Runner has no position and can no longer move to a position.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: The Runner does not have a position while they are not engaged in a run, nor do they maintain their position from one run to the next.

The Runner's current position is a specific element of the sequence of positions, not an index into that sequence. Adding or removing other positions protecting the attacked server does not affect the Runner's position.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a position outward from the Runner's current position is added to the attacked server, the Runner will normally not need to approach or encounter the new piece of ice to reach the server.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If a position inward from the Runner's current position is added to or removed from the attacked server, the ice the Runner will need to approach and/or encounter changes accordingly.
Changes to the piece of ice in the Runner's current position can affect the progression of the run, but they do so differently during an encounter than outside of an encounter.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is uninstalled or moved to another position (protecting this or another server) while it is being approached, the approach ends and the run continues to the Movement Phase.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If a piece of ice currently being approached is swapped with another piece of ice, the Runner remains in their current position and the run remains in the Approach Ice Phase. The Runner is now approaching the new piece of ice occupying that position. Trigger conditions related to a piece of ice being approached are not met for the new ice.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If a piece of ice is uninstalled or derezzed while it is being encountered, the Encounter Phase ends and the run continues to the Movement Phase.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If a piece of ice currently being encountered moves to another position or is swapped with installed ice in another position, the Runner remains with the encountered ice and continues the run from that ice's new position.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: If the piece of ice in the Runner's position is uninstalled, derezzed, moved, or swapped during the Initiation Phase or the Movement Phase, the Runner is not moved and the current timing step of the run does not change.
During a run, abilities can move the Runner directly to a position.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If an ability instructs the Runner to move to a piece of ice in a different position, the Runner's position becomes the position corresponding to that ice, and the server that ice protects becomes the attacked server. The current timing step becomes step 6.9.2, the Approach Ice Phase, or step 6.9.3, the Encounter Ice Phase, according to whether the Runner was directed to approach or encounter the ice.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If an ability instructs the Runner to move to "the outermost position" of a server, that server becomes the attacked server. If there is any ice protecting that server, the Runner's position becomes the position of the outermost such piece of ice, and the current timing step becomes step 6.9.2, the Approach Ice Phase. If there is no ice, the Runner ceases to have a position, and the current timing step becomes step 6.9.4, the Movement Phase.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If an ability instructs the Runner to move to a position during the Success Phase, during the Run Ends Phase, or while there is no run in progress, instead the Runner does nothing. See rule 6.2.5d.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If an ability instructs the Runner to move to and approach a position they are already approaching, instead the Runner does nothing.
The initiation phase sets the parameters for the run and begins the run.
At the start of the Initiation Phase, the Runner announces a server to be the attacked server.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Some abilities state that the Runner "cannot run on" or "cannot initiate a run on" certain servers under certain conditions. These effects refer to the announcement of the attacked server in the Initiation Phase.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Some abilities impose an additional cost to run, either generally or on a particular server. Any costs to run a server must be paid at the time that server is announced as the attacked server.
After the attacked server is announced, credits are added to the Runner's bad publicity fund. See section 10.6 for an explanation of bad publicity.

Some abilities look for particular conditions occurring "during a run" or are restricted to being used "during a run." For purposes of abilities, the run formally begins only after the attacked server is announced and any costs are paid.

When the Initiation Phase completes, the run moves either to the Approach Ice Phase (section 6.4) or the Movement Phase (section 6.6). If there is ice protecting the attacked server, the Runner's position becomes the outermost piece of ice, and the run proceeds to the Approach Ice Phase. If there is no ice protecting the server, then the run moves directly to the Movement Phase.
The approach ice phase gives the Corp the opportunity to rez the ice in the Runner's current position.

For purposes of meeting trigger conditions, the Runner approaching a piece of ice is equivalent to the Approach Ice Phase beginning at that ice's position. Abilities with this trigger condition are subject to rule 9.2.8f.

The paid ability window in step 6.9.2b of the Approach Ice Phase is the only time the Corp can normally rez ice. In this window, the Corp only gains the ability to rez the piece of ice being approached, not any other ice.

When the Approach Ice Phase completes, the run moves either to the Encounter Ice Phase (section 6.5) or the Movement Phase (section 6.6). If the approached piece of ice is rezzed, the Runner encounters it next. If the approached piece of ice is unrezzed or if there is no longer ice installed in that position, then the run moves directly to the Movement Phase.
The encounter ice phase gives the Runner the opportunity to interact with the ice in their current position, then requires the Corp to resolve unbroken subroutines on that ice.

For purposes of meeting trigger conditions, the Runner encountering a piece of ice is equivalent to the Encounter Ice Phase beginning at that ice's position. Abilities with this trigger condition are subject to rule 9.2.8f.
As each encounter begins, each subroutine on the encountered ice gains an "unbroken" status associated with that encounter. See section 9.8 for details.
During the paid ability window in the Encounter Ice Phase (step 6.9.3b), the Runner can break subroutines on the ice. See rule 9.8.5.
After the paid ability window in the Encounter Ice Phase closes, unbroken subroutines on the encountered ice resolve. See section 9.8.7.
At the end of the Encounter Ice Phase, the run continues to the Movement Phase, section 6.6.
Fully Break

rules.label: a.
rules.text: During each encounter, the Runner fully breaks the encountered ice the first time all subroutines on that ice are broken.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Whenever the Runner fully breaks a piece of ice, if all its subroutines were broken using abilities on a single object, that object also fully breaks the ice.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If an encountered piece of ice has no subroutines, the Runner fully breaks it when step 6.9.3b of the encounter begins. No objects fully break the ice in this case.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If the encountered piece of ice gains subroutines after the Runner fully breaks it, the Runner's status of having fully broken the ice remains in place. Conditions that check whether the Runner fully broke the ice will still be met as normal. Breaking the new subroutines will not fully break the ice or meet related conditions again.
Bypass

rules.label: a.
rules.text: When an effect allows the Runner to bypass a piece of ice, the Encounter Ice Phase is aborted and the Runner immediately proceeds to pass that ice.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Most bypass effects occur at the beginning of an encounter and result in steps 6.9.3b and 6.9.3c never occurring, meaning that subroutines on the encountered ice are neither broken nor resolved.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: A few bypass effects can be triggered later. If ice is bypassed in step 6.9.3b, subroutines may or may not have been broken, but step 6.9.3c never occurs so no subroutines resolve. Note that for ice with zero subroutines, the Runner has "broken all subroutines" if and only if step 6.9.3b was reached. See rule 9.12.2d.
Forced Encounters

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If an ability directs the Runner to encounter a piece of ice without first changing their position, resolve an Encounter Ice Phase but do not change the Runner's position, if any. After the encounter, return to the effect that caused the encounter and proceed from there. This type of encounter outside the normal progression of a run is referred to as a forced encounter.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: During a forced encounter, an instruction to end the run is applied to both the Encounter Ice Phase being resolved and the phase from which the additional encounter was initiated. See also rule 6.1.4b.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: An instruction that creates a forced encounter is not finished resolving until the encounter is complete.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: During a forced encounter, if an ability moves the Runner or directs the Runner to approach a piece of ice, that movement resolves and changes the parameters of the underlying run normally, but does not end or interfere with the forced encounter.
The movement phase handles the progression of the run between pieces of ice and after the innermost piece of ice, up to the point when the Runner approaches the attacked server.
If the Movement Phase was reached from the Approach Ice Phase or the Encounter Ice Phase, the Runner passes the ice in their position.
During each Movement Phase, the Runner has the opportunity to jack out. See section 6.1.5.
If the Runner declines to jack out, their position moves to the next inward position if there is one.
If the Runner moves to a new position, the run continues from the Movement Phase to the Approach Ice Phase, section 6.4. The Runner will approach the piece of ice in their new position.

If the Runner does not jack out or return to the Approach Ice Phase, they approach the server. This has no inherent effects, but is referred to by some card abilities. After the Runner approaches the server, the run continues to the Success Phase, section 6.7.
The success phase declares the run successful and allows the Runner to breach the attacked server.
A run during which the runner breaks through the Corp's defenses and reaches the server itself is declared a successful run. This label is frequently referred to by card abilities.
Declaring a run to be successful is not the same as the Success Phase beginning. Accordingly, abilities that have trigger conditions related to a successful run are not subject to rule 9.2.8f.
Many abilities that initiate a run contain a conditional ability with the trigger condition "If successful". This means, "After the run created this way becomes successful".

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If an effect that initiates a run specifies that that run must be made against a specific server or servers, any "If successful" abilities associated with that effect are tied to that server or servers. If the attacked server has changed since the run was initiated, and no longer is a server that could have been chosen for this run, the "If successful" abilities do not meet their trigger conditions.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: "If successful" abilities frequently create lingering effects (see section 9.10) that modify the procedure for accessing cards or replace breaching the attacked server with another effect entirely. These effects apply to the breach permitted by the rules for this run (see rule 6.7.5), and they expire when the run is complete.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If an "If successful" effect gives the Runner an effect they can optionally carry out instead of breaching, that decision is made at the time the breach would begin, in step 6.9.5b.
When the Runner breaches the server, they follow the procedures detailed in section 7.
The run ends phase formalizes the end of the run and prepares the game to return to the timing structure from which the run was initiated.
At the beginning of the Run Ends Phase, the game processes each priority window that was open when the run was ended. This is done according to the following procedure:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a paid ability window was open when the run was ended, the window closes. No player can trigger further paid abilities or resolve other options the window would normally allow (such as rezzing cards).

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If the run was ended during a reaction window opened due to a phase beginning, the reaction window closes, as per rule 9.2.8f. No other pending abilities are resolved.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Any other open priority window is completed normally, except that new timing structures (including a breach that was delayed according to rule 7.3.8) cannot be initiated. If more than one priority window needs to be completed this way, they are resolved in the usual order described in section 9.1.2.
During the Run Ends Phase, if there are any credits remaining in the Runner's bad publicity fund, those credits are returned to the bank.

As part of the Run Ends Phase, the game determines whether the run should be declared an unsuccessful run. This is a label applied to runs in which the Runner failed to reach the server they attacked, and is referred to by card abilities. The run is declared unsuccessful if neither of the following conditions have been met:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If the run reached step 6.9.5, the Success Phase, it is not declared unsuccessful. This is the case regardless of whether the run was actually declared successful.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If the attacked server has ceased to exist, the run is not declared unsuccessful. See rule 8.5.8.

Conditions related to a run ending are not met as soon as an "end the run" effect resolves or at the beginning of the Run Ends Phase. Instead, these conditions are met at step 6.9.6d, when the entire run timing structure is complete. Similarly, static abilities that apply during a run and durations that apply until the end of a run expire at step 6.9.6d.
Initiation Phase

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The Runner announces the attacked server.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Runner adds 1[credit] from the bank to their bad publicity fund for each bad publicity the Corp has.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The run formally begins. Conditions related to the run beginning or initiating are met.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Runner's position is set corresponding to the outermost ice protecting the attacked server, if any.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. (P) (R)

rules.label: f.
rules.text: The Initiation Phase is complete. If the Runner has a position corresponding to a piece of ice, proceed to step 6.9.2, Approach Ice Phase, approaching the piece of ice corresponding to their position. If the Runner has no position or if there is no ice in their position, proceed to step 6.9.4, Movement Phase.
Approach Ice Phase

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The approach begins. Conditions related to the Runner approaching this ice are met.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. Additionally, the Corp can rez the approached piece of ice. (P) (R)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Approach Ice Phase is complete. If the approached piece of ice is rezzed, continue to step 6.9.3, Encounter Ice Phase. Otherwise, proceed to step 6.9.4, Movement Phase.
Encounter Ice Phase

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The encounter begins. Conditions related to the Runner encountering this ice are met.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may only use paid abilities. Subroutines on the encountered ice can be broken during this window. (P)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If there are unbroken subroutines that have not yet resolved this encounter, the Corp resolves the next such subroutine in order. Otherwise, skip to (e).

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Return to (c).

rules.label: e.
rules.text: The Encounter Ice Phase is complete. Continue to step 6.9.4, Movement Phase.
Movement Phase

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If the Runner's position corresponds to a piece of ice, the Runner passes that ice. Conditions related to passing ice are met. If there are no positions more inward than the ice just passed, conditions related to passing all of the ice protecting a server are also met.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may only use paid abilities. (P)

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Runner may choose to jack out, proceeding to step 6.9.6, Run Ends Phase. If the Runner does not, continue to (d).

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Runner's position moves to the next position inward, if any.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: A paid ability window occurs, in which players may use paid abilities and the Corp may rez non-ice cards. (P) (R)

rules.label: f.
rules.text: If the Runner moved to a new position, return to step 6.9.2, Approach Ice Phase, approaching the piece of ice in their new position. If not, continue to (g).

rules.label: g.
rules.text: The Runner approaches the attacked server. Conditions related to the Runner approaching a server are met.

rules.label: h.
rules.text: The Movement Phase is complete. Continue to step 6.9.5, Success Phase.
Success Phase

rules.label: a.
rules.text: The run is declared successful. Conditions related to a successful run are met.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Runner breaches the attacked server.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: The Success Phase is complete. Continue to step 6.9.6, Run Ends Phase.
Run Ends Phase

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Any priority windows that were open when the run moved to this phase are completed or closed as described in section 6.8.2.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Runner returns any remaining credits in the bad publicity fund to the bank.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If the Success Phase was not reached during this run and the attacked server still exists, the run becomes unsuccessful.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: The Run Ends Phase and the run as a whole are both complete.
Accessing is the process of the Corp showing one of their cards to the Runner for potential interaction.

While the Runner is accessing a card, the Runner is allowed to look at that card, even if it would normally not be visible to them. While the Runner is accessing a card, the Corp is allowed to look at it as well, except when the card is being accessed from R&D.
An ability that meets its trigger condition when its source card is accessed is active even if the source card is inactive. See section 9.1.8.
During each access, the Runner has 1 opportunity to use a mid-access ability. This occurs after the reaction window at the beginning of the access, and before the Runner steals an accessed agenda.
The Runner always has the ability "Access → Pay the trash cost of the accessed card: Trash it." This is the basic trash ability.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: All assets and upgrades have trash costs, as do some ice and operations. If a card does not have a trash cost, the Runner cannot pay its trash cost, and therefore the Runner cannot use the basic trash ability during that access.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: The Runner cannot trash or pay the trash cost of a card in the Corp's discard pile, either with the basic trash ability or with other mid-access abilities.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: One card, Mumbad Virtual Tour, has the ability "If the Runner accesses this upgrade while it is installed, they must trash it, if able." When this ability applies, the Runner can use any mid-access ability they have available that trashes the card, but they cannot decline to use a mid-access ability or use one that would not trash the accessed card unless they are unable to pay the cost of any ability that would trash it.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: One card, Neutralize All Threats, has the ability "The first time each turn you access a card with a trash cost, reveal it. You must trash that card by paying its trash cost, if able." When this ability applies, the Runner can only use the basic trash ability. They cannot decline to use a mid-access ability or use a mid-access ability available from a card unless they cannot pay the cost of the basic trash ability.
If, after resolving mid-access abilities, the Runner is still accessing an agenda, they must steal it.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Some abilities can create additional costs to steal an agenda. The Runner can decline to pay such costs and not steal the agenda. See section 1.16.10.
If a card moves to another location while it is being accessed, the access ends immediately.
An "end the run" effect that resolves while a card is being accessed can sometimes end that access. See section 6.1.4.

One card, Information Sifting, uses a method other than a breach to establish a set of cards for the Runner to access. The Runner accesses those cards one at a time in the order of their choice. Each access is performed as a separate instruction. See rule 9.11.4b. Accessing cards in this way is an exception to rule 9.12.2a.

One card, Counter Surveillance, instructs the Runner to access a certain number of cards from a server without mentioning a breach. The procedure for these accesses follows the normal rules for breaching that server except: there is no random access limit if the server is HQ or R&D; and the procedure ends once the designated number of cards have been chosen for access.
The card is accessed. Conditions related to accessing this card are met.
The Runner may use a single mid-access ability, such as the basic trash ability.
If the accessed card is an agenda, the Runner must steal it.
The access is complete. Conditions related to an access ending are met.

Breaching a server is the process of the Runner accessing a particular set of cards associated with that server. Most accesses occur during a breach. Step 6.9.5b of a run calls for the Runner to breach the attacked server, but card abilities can also directly instruct the Runner to breach a server.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: After the Runner accesses a card during a breach, that object remains visible to the Runner for the remainder of the breach.
When the Runner breaches Archives, all the facedown cards in the Corp's discard pile are turned faceup before the Runner accesses any cards.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a card is added to Archives facedown after this step, that card remains facedown for the remainder of the breach, even after it is accessed. The Runner can only look at a facedown card in Archives once they have accessed it.

The cards associated with a breached server that the Runner could potentially access are called Candidates. The set of candidates is compiled from the cards in the root of the breached server and, for central servers, the cards in the zone that corresponds to that server (see rule 4.6.7a). Section 7.4 defines which of these cards are candidates.
During a breach, the Runner is presented with the current candidates. They choose 1 of those cards and access it. This process repeats until there are no longer any candidates.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: When presented with candidates during a breach of HQ, the Runner chooses either a specific candidate that is not in the Corp's hand or to access a random candidate from among the ones in the Corp's hand. A card randomly chosen this way is treated as though the Runner had chosen it.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: One card, Dedicated Neural Net, instructs the Corp to choose which cards the Runner accesses from HQ. While this effect applies, the Runner still chooses candidates that are not in the Corp's hand as normal. Whenever the Runner chooses to access a candidate from the Corp's hand, instead of a candidate being chosen at random, the Corp chooses 1 of those candidates for the Runner to access. The chosen card is still treated as though the Runner had chosen it.

The Runner can only choose candidates from the Corp's hand or deck a limited number of times during a breach of HQ or R&D, respectively. This number is called the Random Access Limit. Before the Runner begins accessing cards during a breach of HQ or R&D, the random access limit for that breach is determined, after which it will not change for the remainder of that breach.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: By default, the random access limit is 1.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If an ability allows the Runner to "access additional cards" during a breach of HQ or R&D, the effect of that ability is to increase the random access limit. Such an ability can only be applied at the beginning of the breach, before the value of the random access limit is set.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If the Runner chooses a candidate in HQ or R&D but does not actually access that card for any reason, that candidate still counts towards reaching the random access limit.
Some abilities count accesses in order to establish a quantity. An ability that counts in this way only includes accesses that are actually performed.
An "end the run" effect that resolves while a server is being breached can sometimes end that breach. See section 6.1.4.

If a server would be breached while a breach is already in progress, instead the new breach takes place when the current breach ends. The effect creating the delayed breach is treated as a conditional ability controlled by the Runner.
The candidates at the beginning of a breach are as follows:

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Each card in the root of the breached server is a candidate.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If the breached server is HQ, each card in the Corp's hand is a candidate.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If the breached server is R&D, the top card of the Corp's deck is a candidate.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If the breached server is Archives, each card in the Corp's discard pile is a candidate.
If at any time the Runner is prohibited from accessing an object, that object ceases to be a candidate. It cannot become a candidate as long as accessing it remains prohibited.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If an ability prohibiting some or all accesses becomes inactive during a breach, candidates are reevaluated to account for the prohibition no longer applying: for each card in or in the root of the breached server, if that object had been prohibited from being accessed by the newly inactive ability, and if no other rule or effect is applicable that would stop that object from being a candidate, then that object becomes a candidate.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Some abilities state that the Runner "cannot access more than 1 card" during a particular run. The effect of this ability is that as long as the Runner has accessed a card during the indicated run, they are prohibited from accessing other cards during that run. The ability has no effect on breaches or candidates until a card has been accessed, and for breaches of HQ and R&D, it never affects the random access limit, even if a card was accessed before the breach began.

Once the Runner chooses a candidate for access, it ceases to be a candidate for the remainder of that breach. It does not matter whether the chosen candidate is actually accessed. As long as the card is chosen, it ceases to be a candidate.

When the random access limit is reached during a breach of HQ or R&D, all candidates in the zone corresponding to the breached server cease to be candidates, and no cards in that zone can become candidates for the remainder of that breach. See section 7.3.5.
If a candidate leaves the breached server, it ceases to be a candidate. Note that the moved card could be a new object, which could be eligible to become a new candidate if appropriate.
Cards entering a server while a breach is in progress can become candidates.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a card enters the root of a server during a breach of that server, the Runner decides whether that card becomes a candidate during step 10.3.1j of the next checkpoint. If the Runner chooses for the card not to become a candidate, then that object cannot be a candidate for the remainder of the breach.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: If a card enters the Corp's hand during a breach of HQ while the random access limit has not yet been reached, that card becomes a candidate.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: If a card enters the Corp's deck during a breach of R&D, that card could become a candidate (either at that time or later in the breach), depending on the random access limit and its position within the deck. See section 7.4.7.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: If a card enters the Corp's discard pile during a breach of Archives, that card becomes a candidate. See also rule 7.3.2a.

During a breach of R&D, the Runner is presented with 1 candidate from the Corp's deck at a time in turn, working down from the top of the deck. Cards are made candidates 1 at a time until the access limit is reached.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: After the Runner chooses a candidate from the Corp's deck and whenever any cards enter, leave, or are reordered within the Corp's deck, all cards in the Corp's deck cease to be candidates. Then, if the random access limit has not been reached, the topmost eligible card in the deck becomes a candidate. A card is eligible for this purpose if the Runner has not already chosen to access that object and is not prohibited from accessing that object in this breach.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: One card, Showing Off, allows the Runner to access cards from the bottom of R&D. While this effect applies, candidates in the Corp's deck are presented working up from the bottom: treat rule 7.4.1c as if it said "bottom" instead of "top" and rule 7.4.7a as if it said "bottommost" instead of "topmost".
Breaching the server formally begins. Conditions related to breaching this server are met.
If the breached server is Archives, turn all cards in the Corp's discard pile faceup.
If the breached server is HQ or R&D, determine the limit to how many times the Runner can choose a candidate from the Corp's hand or deck.
The Runner chooses a candidate. If they cannot, skip to step 7.5.7.
The Runner accesses the chosen card.
Return to step 7.5.4.
The breach is complete. Conditions related to the breach ending are met.

An agenda, asset, upgrade, or piece of ice is unrezzed if it is installed and facedown. An asset, upgrade, or piece of ice is rezzed if it is installed and faceup. Runner cards, faceup agendas, operations, events, and counters are neither rezzed nor unrezzed.
To rez an unrezzed card is to turn it faceup.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Some paid ability windows allow the Corp to rez assets and upgrades. See section 9.2.7. The paid ability window at step 6.9.2b of a run allows the Corp to rez ice.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Card abilities can direct or allow the Corp to rez cards at other times.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Agendas cannot be rezzed.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: Before rezzing a card, the Corp must pay that card's rez cost. This includes both rezzing in a paid ability window and rezzing through a card ability. Card abilities can modify or ignore rez costs, but must state this explicitly.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: To resolve rezzing a card, the Corp pays its rez cost (accounting for any modifiers or additional costs), a checkpoint occurs (as required by rule 10.3.4), then the Corp turns the card faceup. For purposes of meeting trigger conditions, the card is considered to be rezzed at the conclusion of this process.
To derez a rezzed card is to turn it facedown.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Cards are only derezzed by card effects.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: There is no inherent cost associated with derezzing a card.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: Derezzing a card is instantaneous and has no component steps.
Some abilities can install Runner cards facedown or turn already-installed Runner cards facedown.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Installed Runner cards that are facedown do not have any characteristics (name, card type, faction, cost, subtypes, influence, etc), and their abilities are not active.

rules.label: b.
rules.text: Facedown installed Runner cards are distinct. The origin of each such card (when and how it was installed facedown, or what faceup installed card was turned facedown) is open information.

rules.label: c.
rules.text: After a facedown Runner card enters the heap, it is turned faceup.

rules.label: d.
rules.text: A Runner card turned facedown is not considered to be uninstalled and simply remains in the play area.

rules.label: e.
rules.text: If an installed facedown Runner card is turned faceup, the card regains its printed characteristics and it becomes active. Turning an installed facedown Runner card faceup does not meet the trigger conditions of "when installed" abilities.

rules.label: f.
rules.text: Runner cards are never considered rezzed or unrezzed.
A movement is a way that cards change their zone or location following special rules. The movements are: arrange, draw, forfeit, install, play, search, score, steal, swap, and trash.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: Other terms that change the locations of cards are not movements. If an ability directs a player to "add" or "move" cards to 1 or more locations, simply put those cards in the indicated locations. If an ability or game rule directs a player to "discard", "set aside", or "remove from the game" 1 or more cards, simply put those cards in their owner's discard pile, the set-aside zone, or the removed-from-game zone, respectively.

If a replacement effect modifies the effects of a movement, but does not replace the entire movement by name, the modified effect is still an occurrence of that movement and can still meet trigger conditions relating to that type of movement.

rules.label: a.
rules.text: If a movement is replaced or prevented entirely or otherwise cannot be carried out, that movement does not take place and conditions related to that type of movement are not met.
To arrange a set of cards is to reposition them among their current locations. The full rules for arranging are detailed in section 8.3.
To draw a given number of cards is to move that many cards from the top of a player's deck to their hand. The full rules for drawing cards are detailed in section 8.4.

To forfeit an agenda is to move it from a player's score area to the removed-from-game zone. When a player forfeits an agenda, its agenda points no longer contribute to that player's score, and any objects hosted on it are trashed.
To install a card is to move it from its current zone to the play area. The full rules for installing cards are detailed in section 8.5.

To play an event or operation is to move it from its current zone to the play area, resolve its play abilities, and then trash it. The full rules for playing events and operations are detailed in section 8.6.
To search is to look at a specified zone and potentially set aside cards from that zone. The full rules for searching are detailed in section 8.7.
To score an agenda is to move it from its current zone to the Corp's score area. The full rules for scoring are detailed in section 1.17.
To steal an agenda is to move it from its current zone to the Runner's score area. The full rules for stealing are detailed in section 1.17.
To swap a pair of cards is to move each card to the other's location simultaneously. The full rules for swapping are detailed in section 8.8.
